virals.name: LanceBuildsIt
virals.text:
A build-in-public habit worth stealing: post what you cut, not just what you shipped.

"Shipped X" tells people you're busy. "Cut Y because nobody who signed up ever got to it" tells them how you decide, and that's the part other builders and future customers actually learn from.

virals.name: LevenkoN
virals.text:
There were people making images long before #AI.
Then came those who suddenly discovered they were “artists” the moment the tool arrived.

Yet access to a tool is no proof of artistry. Neither is a follower count, nor the chorus of “awesome” and “amazing” beneath a post. Applause

patterns: nobody is watching, so go: 'I regret to inform you that nobody cares... Go do the thing' (Bloom 202k views, 6.6k likes, 1.4k bookmarks, top post of the day)
subtraction before addition: 'what must be discarded to make space for your new endeavors?' (James Clear 59k, 1.1k likes, 390 bookmarks)

your circle sets your ceiling: 'How to stay poor: think everyone is broke because everyone you know is broke' (Hormozi 73k, 2.5k likes), a sequel to his 'only sell to broke people' hit from the weekend

the one-year bet: 'people are terrified of one year on their own, so they spend 50 years doing something they hate' (Welsh 17k, 138 replies) and 'work insanely hard while life is simple enough to let you' (15k)
finishing as identity: 'You are not your goals. You are the things you finish.' (Codie 19k, 622 likes, highest like rate on the list)
beginner's mind as an edge: 'your entire life will change when you become a beginner again' (Bloom 23k)

AI as a working tool, not a threat: GaryVee 'what's your biggest use of AI right now?' clip (50k); outsider heat stays on the AI stack for a one-person business (388k on a newsletter post) and an AI-team prompt (10k)
selling formats: GaryVee's live-shopping article (24k) and Codie's delegation brief for scaling a business (17k, 202 bookmarks)
virals_narrative: Quieter Monday. Sahil Bloom's 'I regret to inform you that nobody cares... go do the thing' led everything at 202k views and 6.6k likes. Alex Hormozi followed up his weekend hit with 'How to stay poor: think everyone is broke because everyone you know is broke' (73k), and James Clear's Monday question about what you must give up to make space for something new pulled 59k and 390 bookmarks. Justin Welsh's one-year bet post drew the most replies on the board relative to its size, and Codie Sanchez's 'You are not your goals. You are the things you finish.' had the best like rate. Dan Koe, Jack Butcher, Austin Kleon and Rory Sutherland posted nothing original in the window. Outsider posts were thin again; the AI one-person-business stack is still the only big outsider theme.

drafts.draft_en:
Nobody is waiting for your album.

That sounds harsh. It's actually the kindest thing I know.

Nobody's waiting, so nobody's judging.
You're free to make the weird one.
Ship it. Learn. Make the next.

The silence isn't rejection.
It's room.
drafts.video_tip: One take at the piano or desk, lights low. Say the first line to camera, then play four bars of something unfinished. Burn in the last two lines as captions.
drafts.pattern: nobody cares, go do the thing (Bloom) + creative career

drafts.draft_en:
Every new creative project I start costs me something old.

This year it was saying yes to every jingle.
The money was fine.
The time was the price.

Before you add the dream, name what you're giving up for it.

If you can't name it, you haven't started.
drafts.video_tip: Hands-only shot writing two columns on paper, 'adding' and 'giving up'. Fill the second column first. Voiceover reads the post. Under 30 seconds.
drafts.pattern: subtract to make space (James Clear) + creative business

drafts.draft_en:
Most artists undercharge because everyone around them undercharges.

If your whole circle sells for ₹2,000, ₹20,000 feels like greed.

It isn't. It's just a room you haven't been in.

Spend time with people who sell the work properly.
Your prices will follow your friends.
drafts.video_tip: Walk-and-talk outside the studio, phone at chest height. Hold up one finished piece when you say the price. Keep it to a single take.
drafts.pattern: your circle sets your ceiling (Hormozi) + selling

drafts.draft_en:
Give yourself one year.

Not forever. One year of making the thing you actually care about, in public, for money.

If it fails, you've lost a year and learned a craft.
If you never try, you've lost the other forty.

One year is cheap.
drafts.video_tip: Calendar on the wall, mark today with a red pen and draw a line twelve months out. Speak to camera beside it. End on the empty months.
